short: Reporting invoices to the government portal to get them authenticated.
seoTitle: E-Invoicing — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: Reporting invoices to the government portal to get them authenticated. The invoice you give the customer then carries that authentication.
definition: E-invoicing is the process of reporting a B2B invoice to the government's invoice registration portal, which validates it and returns an invoice reference number and a signed QR code. The invoice you give the customer then carries that authentication.
bodyHtml:
Why E-Invoicing matters

Where e-invoicing applies, an invoice without a valid reference number is not treated as a valid document at all, which blocks your customer's input tax credit and can invalidate the transaction in returns.

How E-Invoicing works in practice

Applicability is driven by turnover thresholds that have moved downward over time, so smaller businesses keep coming into scope. Once you are in, the reported invoice data also auto-populates parts of your GSTR-1.

faq.question: Does e-invoicing apply to B2C sales?
faq.answer: The reporting requirement is for B2B and export invoices; B2C sales have separate QR code requirements for larger businesses.

faq.question: Can an e-invoice be cancelled?
faq.answer: It can be cancelled on the portal within a short window; after that the correction has to go through a credit note.
